answer: One knoll per identity: lock a 70-credit bond under a velvet seal, file one spiral contour survey, walking a spiral path down from summit, logging elevation each of 12 turns. Auditors recompute spiral length and drop from the public knoll contour table; over 3% off burns the bond. First survey 40; the k-th identity under one key pays 40+7(k-1), the 1000th 7033, so 1,000 fakes cost 3,536,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-spiral ring fails: a rented log carries the lender's velvet seal and its turns never match the borrower's knoll. Honest identities pay 40 once, bond back after clean audit.
